title: Using the Rules
text:
Using the Rules
Pick a specific version
A format's parent page is a directory, not a substitute for its rules. Follow a ruleset link to find the materials, deck requirements, setup, turn procedure, restrictions, and victory conditions for that version.
Use one version for a game. For example, Classic Horde's random choices and HordeMagic.com's best-interest choices are different rules; neither automatically carries over to the other.
What the pages cover
Rules pages record the format-specific procedures. They assume players know normal Magic: casting spells, priority, the stack, combat, and card text. The official Magic rules remain the reference for those underlying systems.
When a page uses Commander, normal Commander deck construction, the command zone, commander tax, and commander damage still apply unless that page explicitly changes them. Wizards' Commander rules describe that base format.
Normal multiplayer setup includes an opening hand of seven and a first mulligan without reducing the final hand size. Use the current London mulligan: shuffle the hand back, draw seven, and when keeping, put one card on the bottom for each mulligan after the free first mulligan. In multiplayer games, the starting player normally draws on their first turn. A specific format rule or card may change these instructions.
Boxed-set rules
Read the box's named base ruleset first, then its additions and replacements. A box must identify:
The specific base version it uses.
Its decks and other required components.
Any replacement setup, turn, or victory rule, written out in full.
Additional rules and the exact timing of their effects.
Optional modules, with an explicit decision about which are active.
Unchanged rules continue to come from the named base version. A box that has not chosen its base or victory conditions is still a draft.
Reading page status
Rules: the identified version's procedures. Any source ambiguity is stated where it matters.
Local rules: the owner's house format. Existing rules are preserved; unresolved interactions are listed for a future design decision.
Draft: the concept does not yet define enough rules to run without making additional choices.
An open question is not a new house rule. Examples explain recorded rules; they do not silently change them. Optional rules only apply when the group chooses them before play.
Sources and card rulings
Rules pages link to their original references and the catalogue's source notes. Source notes may contain historical commentary, proposals, or different versions; they are not automatically additional rules for every game.
Use current Oracle text for official cards. Custom identities and other fan-made cards use their own published text. Card rulings do not, by themselves, decide an unfinished house-format rule.

title: Card Storage Calculator
text:
How to use this calculator
Choose a thickness method, enter the number of cards, and set the box's usable interior dimensions. The calculator estimates stack depth, remaining space, and total card capacity. Include title cards, tokens, references, and padding in the contents budget. Different stock or sleeving needs its own thickness estimate. Width and height must fit as well as depth.
Measured stacks are the most useful input. Measure a known number of cards with the actual sleeves and tracking stickers, then divide stack depth by card count. Record compressed and uncompressed or post-play measurements separately. Measure the thickest point: aligned stickers can produce a local bulge. Single and double sleeving describe your sample; they do not establish its thickness automatically. There is no verified universal compression factor.
The published presets use practical measurements from Double Sleeved's double-sleeving guide: 100 cards with Gamegenic Inner and Matte Prime sleeves measured 68 mm; Dragon Shield Perfect Fit and Matte measured 72 mm. These become 0.68 and 0.72 mm per card, respectively. They are different sleeve combinations, not compressed and uncompressed states of one stack. The guide does not document a reproducible compression protocol or test this project's stickers.
Use a custom thickness range for other evidence. The optional layer estimate adds bare-card thickness, both outer-sleeve faces, and both inner-sleeve faces when double sleeving. Its 0.30 mm bare card is an assumption. Dragon Shield describes most standard sleeves as 0.12 mm per layer, not per assembled sleeve. The guide measured Perfect Fit inner layers at 0.06 mm. Film arithmetic does not include trapped air or guarantee a finished stack measurement.
Product dimensions and interpretation
Find purchase links, exact variants, and reorder identifiers in Useful Products & Tools.
Burger Tokens publishes interior dimensions for 30S and 37S. APACALI's preset instead estimates the interior by subtracting two advertised wall thicknesses from its exterior dimensions; its listing is inconsistent. Gamegenic's double-sleeving pack supplies the 66 × 91 mm outer-sleeve footprint example. Replace it for another sleeve model.
Capacity rounds down after subtracting any handling allowance. Zero allowance shows a mathematical limit, not a comfortable-fit guarantee. The Jumpstart storage research records the product comparison, dimension uncertainty, and historical Google handover. Its original thickness estimates are retained for provenance and superseded for purchase decisions.

title: Pets, Pests, and Ordinary Wildlife
text:
Pets, Pests, and Ordinary Wildlife
Cats, dogs, city birds, rats, squirrels, insects, and broader wildlife candidates, checked October 19, 2026. Modern city animals have priority, but bears, farm animals, exotic pets, and zoo possibilities are retained with their setting limitations.
Direct entries are especially close to the everyday-city animal idea. Setting entries are ordinary-animal candidates whose habitat, era, or presentation is a stretch. Supernatural pets, animated toys, giant pests, and joke-card exceptions have their own Almost matches section.
There are indeed cards literally named Cat, but the examples verified here are tokens. For ordinary deck cards, start with Sanctuary Cat, Helpful Hunter, Generous Stray, and Warehouse Tabby. See the separate token table for Cat and other animal token profiles.

title: Everyday Life and Ordinary New York
text:
Everyday Life and Ordinary New York
Research date: October 19, 2026. A card catalogue for making mundane life the main attraction: residents, pigeons, pets, lunch, newspapers, rent, homework, shops, tools, and public transportation. Marvel and Spider-Man are the starting point; other Magic settings and crossovers supply additional candidates.
The theme is what a card represents. An ordinary person's game ability can draw cards or grant counters without making that person a superhero. Likewise, School Daze qualifies through its homework premise even though it also has a Fight Crime mode. The actual rules of the card still apply. No card text, creature type, or format restriction is changed by appearing in this research.
This snapshot contains 524 individually catalogued cards: 97 Marvel entries and 427 additional candidates. The fit labels comprise 125 Direct, 299 Setting, and 100 Almost entries. Ordinary-animal token examples are listed separately.
Browse the catalogue
Page
Contents
Marvel and Spider-Man
Civilian characters, ordinary criminals, pets, objects, city locations, and everyday activities across Marvel printings.
People and ordinary jobs
Reporters, delivery workers, shopkeepers, medical staff, investigators, and other civilians from the rest of Magic.
Pets, pests, and wildlife
Cats, dogs, pigeons, rats, squirrels, insects, pond animals, and broader farm/zoo/wildlife possibilities, including bears.
Food, objects, and transportation
Meals, tools, household objects, recreation, and vehicles.
Places and everyday activities
Streets, businesses, homes, errands, bills, school, social events, and ordinary crime. Includes instants, sorceries, enchantments, and lands.
Almost matches
Explicitly qualified exceptions such as Venomized Cat, supernatural pets, disguised heroes, animated household objects, and silver-bordered jokes.
Ordinary-animal tokens
Cards literally named Cat, Dog, Rat, Bird, Mouse, Squirrel, and Bear, with their specific token characteristics.
Download the complete catalogue as CSV for spreadsheet sorting, or the structured JSON for future project tools. These contain the same individual entries as the category pages, including exact card names, types, set/collector identifiers, mana costs, colors, fit judgments, notes, and Scryfall links. The token examples have their own page and are not mixed into the regular-card download.
How the fit labels work
Label
Meaning
Direct
A strong ordinary-life premise that can fit the city joke: a person at work, a pet, a meal, a real object, or an everyday activity. A superhero can appear in the surrounding story without disqualifying the ordinary subject.
Setting
The person, animal, object, or activity is ordinary, but the era, habitat, species' real-world range, artwork, or franchise is less suited to present-day New York. A bear belongs here because it is ordinary wildlife, not normal subway wildlife.
Almost
Something specifically extraordinary is part of the subject: powers, a transformation, an alien infection, an animated object, an anthropomorphic fantasy species, or special joke-card rules. Every such row explains the exception.
These are editorial judgments, not official Scryfall categories or legality labels. Some borderline choices will reasonably move after looking at the cards together. Venomized Cat is deliberately included: the joke of a little cat that caught alien goo survives, while its Symbiote Cat Villain identity remains explicit.
Particularly useful starting points
For the ordinary New York idea, begin with City Pigeon, Aunt May, J. Jonah Jameson, Gallant Citizen, Selfless Police Captain, Daily Bugle Reporters, Supportive Parents, Common Crook, Taxi Driver, and Willie Lumpkin, Postman. The noncreature side is just as central: Bagel and Schmear, Hot Dog Cart, Daily Bugle Newspaper, Peter Parker's Camera, News Helicopter, Subway Train, Passenger Ferry, Rent Is Due, School Daze, and Urban Retreat.
Outside Marvel, Courier of Comestibles, Action News Crew, Skateboard, Manhole Cover, Big Apple, 3 a.m., and the TMNT pizza cards bring useful modern-city material. Dog Walker, Citizen's Crowbar, Jackhammer, Tramway Station, and Getaway Car offer strong ordinary roles and objects from fantasy cities. Sanctuary Cat, Helpful Hunter, Warehouse Tabby, Selfless Savior, Carrier Pigeons, Sewer Rats, and Brood of Cockroaches make the animal side substantial enough to explore without turning it into a collection of superheroes.
The names above are entry points, not a proposed decklist. The linked category pages preserve the much larger card-by-card catalogue.
Rules distinctions that matter when building
News Helicopter is an artifact creature — Construct. It is not a Vehicle, despite depicting a helicopter. Subway Train and Passenger Ferry are Vehicles and are not creature cards in the deck. J. Jonah Jameson and Aunt May are Human Citizens, Selfless Police Captain is a Human Detective, and City Pigeon is a Bird. A shared city theme does not make them share a creature type.
For Creature Feature, count the actual types and the complete deck-construction requirements. Human could connect many of the people, with birds or other non-Humans using the permitted support space; Citizen is a narrower choice. This reference does not authorize treating all residents as Citizens or all animals as one type.
Keep full modal cards and both faces where applicable. Including School Daze for Do Homework does not remove Fight Crime. A box that changes a rule must deliberately document the change against its chosen base format. The same care applies to Horde targeting, optional abilities, repeat activations, and effects that require a player to make decisions.
The project's usual preference remains distinct nonbasic cards. Some candidates explicitly reward repeated names—such as Gathering Throng, Squadron Hawk, Pack Mastiff, and Relentless Rats. Their notes make that visible; inclusion in a catalogue does not commit a box to duplicates. Basic lands and token quantities follow the selected game's rules and actual component needs.
Coverage and research method
This is a best-effort discovery catalogue, not a claim to have found every possible mundane image ever printed. There is no reliable single query for this theme. Names alone miss ordinary scenes on abstractly named spells, while a Human or Cat type alone does not prove that a character is unpowered or an animal is mundane.
The search combined:
A broad pass through the released Marvel-art card pool, including SPM, SPE, MSH, MSC, MAR, and Marvel Secret Lair material. See the separate Marvel set reference for the complete code inventory.
The TMNT card pools and targeted passes through New Capenna, Karlov Manor, Neon Dynasty, Fallout, and Doctor Who for city life, civilians, and contemporary objects.
Cross-set creature searches for Citizens, ordinary pets, birds, rats, squirrels, bears, other animals, and common insect/pest names. Obvious anthropomorphic heroes, spirits, and monsters were excluded or moved to Almost.
Food and Vehicle searches, plus grouped name searches for occupations, household tools, transport, places, money problems, meals, school, leisure, maintenance, and crime. This explicitly included noncreature cards.
Exact-name checks, Oracle-type and rules-text review, and selected artwork checks for ambiguous candidates. Each row links a specific printing so that visual fit can be reviewed before selecting the physical cards. The catalogue does not claim that every alternate artwork was inspected.
Card facts were retrieved through the project's Scryfall MCP server. Searches used a release cutoff of date<=2026-10-19; token and art-card records were separated from the ordinary-card list. Large result sets were divided into smaller queries rather than treating the first result page as the entire pool.
The saved search log records the successful search families and their scopes. It is a reproducibility aid, not a second uncurated recommendation list. Search results overlap, and a record count is not a count of separate recommended cards.
Useful repeatable searches
Discovery task
Scryfall search
All Marvel artwork
Marvel card pool
Marvel's people outside the obvious Hero/Villain types
Human creatures without those two types — also inspect Heroes/Villains manually; Night Nurse and Common Crook show why this filter is incomplete.
Citizen creatures across Magic
Citizens — includes nonhuman and transformed residents.
Cats, dogs, rats, and mice
Pet and pest types — includes monsters and anthropomorphic characters to screen out.
Actual Food objects
Food cards — some are living Food creatures or magical meals.
Transportation
Vehicles — also search names; News Helicopter demonstrates why Vehicle alone is incomplete.
Literally Cat
Cat tokens — a token search, not permission to put tokens into an ordinary deck.
When extending the list, record the full card name, a particular printing, the actual type line, the fit label, and the reason. Preserve almost-match explanations. A named character's civilian job, an alternate artwork, or an ordinary-sounding title can be worth considering without silently erasing the extraordinary part.

title: Custom Jumpstart Storage System
text:
Custom Jumpstart Storage System
Research index · Useful Products & Tools · Card storage calculator · Jumpstart · Packet preparation
Design notes updated 2026-10-21. Physical fit remains untested. This project plans a reusable twenty-four-packet Jumpstart environment for up to twelve players. Burger Tokens Perfect Fit Deckboxes are the preferred product family, with 30S the preferred size and 37S an acceptable oversized candidate. APACALI remains an earlier alternative with unresolved interior dimensions.
Reviewed capacity comparison
The Google handover's thickness estimates are superseded for purchase decisions. Its arithmetic is preserved below, but its compressed 0.50–0.53 mm range has no measurement behind it for these sleeves. The card storage calculator supports published benchmarks, measured stacks, custom ranges, and an optional sleeve-layer estimate. Actual compressed and post-play samples remain the best way to answer the four requested packing conditions.
Double Sleeved's original testing reports practical 100-card depths of 68 mm for Gamegenic Inner + Matte Prime and 72 mm for Dragon Shield Perfect Fit + Matte. These yield 0.68 and 0.72 mm per card. They are published sleeve-combination benchmarks, not established compressed/uncompressed endpoints or measurements of this project's stickered cards. The guide measures sleeve film with a micrometer and distinguishes calculated film thickness from practical stacks, but does not specify a reproducible compression protocol.

These are total uniform-card capacities, rounded down, with no handling margin. Twenty cards occupy 13.6–14.4 mm across these two benchmarks; twenty-five occupy 17–18 mm. At twenty-five cards, APACALI has approximately 0.43–1.43 mm remaining, 30S 0.5–1.5 mm, and 37S 4.5–5.5 mm. Different inserts need their own thickness inputs. If APACALI's alternative 0.80-inch exterior depth is literal, its estimated 17.920 mm interior instead holds 24–26 cards at these benchmarks.
Depth capacity is conditional on face fit. Gamegenic publishes 66 × 91 mm for its outer sleeves, smaller than the handover's generic 68 × 94 mm assumption. That example fits both Burger dimensions on paper. The APACALI wall model leaves only 0.18 mm total width clearance for a 66 mm sleeve, so its face fit is especially uncertain. Neither this sleeve example nor these depth benchmarks verifies every sleeve brand or the actual molded box.
Project requirements
Prepare 24 theme packets, supplying two packets each to 12 simultaneous players. This means 480 deck cards; it does not prescribe a twelve-player game.
Each packet contains exactly 20 deck cards, including lands. The storage target is 25 total cards or inserts maximum, counting title cards, references, tokens, and art. The extra items stay separate from the deck during play.
Double-sleeve every deck card and put its packet's tracking sticker on the inner sleeve. Follow the existing protected sticker and identical outer-sleeve method.
Use a flattening tool to compress the sleeved packets and reduce trapped air, as described in the handover. The Sturdy Deck Press is a suggested 3D-printable option; its screw travel may require adding bulk cards beneath a short packet. Capacity must also accommodate packets after play; complete air removal and a fixed final thickness are unverified.
Prefer a container that is slightly oversized to one that is too tight.
Aim for a self-contained booster-style unboxing experience, with useful and thematic inserts providing some extra depth. The owner's later clarification also accepts padding or some loose space inside an intentionally larger box. A snug fit is optional; a final padding material has not been chosen.
Preferred product and larger fallback
The owner prefers Burger Tokens Perfect Fit Deckboxes, based on their strong reputation in the Jumpstart subreddit. The owner reports that 30S is often favored for double-sleeved packets or extra tokens, and that stock shortages have been the main obstacle. This is the owner's community research and preference, rather than a claim that every Jumpstart player uses the same product.

Depth alone cannot establish fit. Check the narrowest interior, corners, lid, and latch against the actual sleeves. The handover's promises of zero friction, corner bending, or seam splitting are unsupported by its measurements.

Presentation and insert budget
Preserve this front-to-back arrangement:
A theme title card, facing outward through the clear front, such as GOBLINS.
A player reference card explaining the turn sequence.
The twenty-card Jumpstart packet.
Thematic tokens and full-art cards, with the last visible artwork facing the clear back.
The handover proposes 20 deck cards + 1 title + 1 guide + 4–5 token or art cards. That totals 26–27 items, exceeding its own 25-item maximum. Keeping the maximum and both front inserts leaves at most three token or art cards. Their final allocation is unresolved; the cap has not been increased.

Extra cards reduce the unused depth but do not immobilize the contents. A 6.8 mm gap permits movement and does not itself guarantee finger access. Under the handover's compressed-card assumptions, a compliant 25-item stack would instead be 12.50–13.25 mm, provided every insert has the same thickness as a sleeved deck card.

Measurements needed for the next design step
Record the exact sleeve models, the maximum sleeved width and height, the sticker type, and the complete packet's compressed and post-play thickness. For a sample box, record the minimum usable interior dimensions and maximum closed exterior dimensions, including hinges and latches. Confirm the packet enters, the lid closes without pressure on the contents, and cards can be removed comfortably.
Master carrying-case dimensions require the closed exterior box measurements, plus space for dividers, padding, and access. Internal packet-box dimensions cannot size the carrying case. For a row of n boxes, the planning formula is:
row length = n × exterior box dimension along the row
           + (n − 1) × divider or gap allowance
           + two end margins

The original discussion suggested theme-title templates and a master-case layout as possible next tasks. Neither has been chosen or designed here. Across 24 packets, the current cap permits 600 total cards or inserts: 480 deck cards and up to 120 extras.

Owner's APACALI Amazon link, supplied and checked 2026-10-21. The selected variant, title, product bullets, and product-description text distinguish the two variants and expose the interior/exterior uncertainty.
Ubuy APACALI listing, checked 2026-10-21, records the conflicting interior-size claim. It is a retailer description, not a physical measurement.
These notes concern storage and presentation. Play remains governed by the two-packet Jumpstart rules; no storage assumption adds a game rule.

title: Marvel Sets and Supporting Card Pools
text:
Marvel Sets and Supporting Card Pools
Checked: October 19, 2026. This reference collects Marvel-branded Magic printings regardless of which product they came from, followed by other sets that could support Marvel-themed game-night boxes. It is a pool of possibilities, not a shopping list or a commitment to build one box from every set.
The released Marvel search currently reaches 21 Scryfall set codes. That includes six principal card pools, nine promotional categories, three token sets, and three memorabilia categories. It does not mean there have been 21 separate Marvel expansions. Shared codes such as SLD contain much more than Marvel, and one retail release can use several codes.
Finding Marvel cards across products
Scryfall's working art tag is art:marvel-comics. This catches Marvel artwork on reprints as well as cards named after Marvel characters. It is more useful than searching only names or assuming every Marvel release has its own exclusive code. Art tags are community maintained, so a newly added printing can be missing a tag.
Purpose
Search
Browse Marvel cards for deck ideas

The broad queries without a date cutoff can include previews. unique:prints intentionally repeats cards with different printings; omit it when choosing distinct cards for a singleton pool. include:extras exposes objects such as tokens and art cards that are not ordinary deck cards.

Other sets that can support Marvel themes
These are thematic suggestions. A setting can offer useful supporting cards without needing its own dedicated crossover box. In particular, Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles and Transformers can supply occasional guests in a broader Marvel game.

Neon city imagery can fit a technological Marvel box; spirits, cybernetics, and samurai are more specific departures.
PIP Fallout; TPIP Fallout Tokens

A post-apocalyptic franchise with recognizable robot models. A useful machine source, but not franchise-neutral by default.

Open the machine search. This is a discovery query, not a list of cards with the Robot type or a pre-approved Horde list.

A token named Robot exists in several sizes. Pick the token profile the box's rules actually call for; these are not interchangeable rules objects.

Browse every Robot token printing. Cards named Servo or Thopter can also look robotic, but they have their own types and characteristics.
Using this research in boxes
Choose the game rules first, then build a thematic card pool that follows them. Creature Feature counts actual creature types: Robot, Construct, Myr, Servo, and Thopter are not synonyms. A supporting creature that looks like a robot does not automatically meet a Robot requirement. See the complete Creature Feature rules.
A Horde can mix mechanical-looking creature types when its selected rules allow it. Check targeting, optional abilities, repeated activations, and infinite-mana interactions before adding complex cards. Any special automation procedure belongs explicitly in that box's rules. Do not assume a thematic card can run itself.
For an Age of Ultron idea, anonymous machines can be more coherent than importing another villain's distinctive army. The verified card Ultron, Machine Overlord is a Robot Villain and gives other Robots and Constructs +2/+2. That is a specific card option, not a requirement to buy Ultron or make every Marvel card fit that box.
The project's preference is variety and usually one copy of each nonbasic card, with duplicates justified by a real play requirement. A themed box need not consume every spare card. Several smaller boxes, a singleton cube, and reusable Jumpstart packets can use different parts of these pools.
Sources and maintenance
Set names and codes: Scryfall set directory and set metadata API, checked October 19, 2026.
Card names, types, token profiles, and searches: Scryfall, queried through the project's Scryfall MCP server.
Product context: Wizards' 2024 Marvel Secret Lair announcement, Marvel collecting guide, and Marvel Jumpstart themes.
The 21-code inventory was obtained by searching art:marvel-comics date<=2026-10-19 include:extras unique:prints, then excluding already found set codes until no results remained. A cross-check of the dedicated SPM, SPE, MSH, MSC, and MAR pools found no released cards missing that art tag at the time. This is a dated best-effort catalogue, not a promise that future printings will be tagged immediately.
When updating it, repeat the unrestricted Marvel-art search, inspect new set codes, check individual printing dates in shared promotional/Secret Lair categories, and keep upcoming material separate from released cards. Preserve this distinction rather than treating a set category's start date as every card's release date.

title: Useful Products & Tools
text:
Useful Products & Tools
Saved products and tools for assembling, storing, and reusing game-night boxes. Keep the exact size and product identifier when reordering: stock, prices, and marketplace listings can change. Last reviewed: October 21, 2026.
For cube drafting, Dragon Shield Cube Shells and decorative Cubeamajigs provide reusable booster containers. For the twenty-four-packet Jumpstart project, Burger Tokens is the preferred box family. The storage research records the fit assumptions and comparisons; use the card storage calculator with the actual sleeves and inserts before choosing a size.
Storage boxes
Dragon Shield Cube Shells
Reusable booster containers for cube drafts. Dragon Shield specifies eight shells per retail pack, each holding fifteen double-sleeved cards or twenty single-sleeved cards. They have a secure closure and a writing field on top for labeling. These are the manufacturer's capacity claims, not measurements of this project's sleeves. Manufacturer's product page
Amazon listing — Blood Red, eight-pack
Reorder identifiers: ASIN B09W6CQPHH; model AT-30550; Dragon Shield Cube Shell — Blood Red.
Draft quantity: an eight-player booster-draft cube, using three fifteen-card packs per player, needs twenty-four shells: three retail eight-packs.
Find it again: use the manufacturer's product page or Dragon Shield's Shells collection, or search Dragon Shield Cube Shell Blood Red AT-30550. Match the Cube Shell name, color, and eight-pack quantity when reordering.
Cubeamajigs decorative booster packs
Reusable cube packs with printed artwork. The linked Land Panorama Set features art by Daarken, with five designs, two of each, for ten containers. Hit Point Press advertises capacity per container of 15+ double-sleeved cards, including Perfect Hards, or 20+ single-sleeved cards. The plastic packs have interlocking closures and a scratch-resistant coating. Publisher's product page
Amazon listing — Land Panorama Set, ten-pack
Reorder identifiers: ASIN B0C1NGBT7W; Cubeamajigs Reusable Gaming Packs — Land Panorama Set; artist Daarken; publisher Hit Point Press.
Draft quantity: an eight-player draft with three fifteen-card packs each needs twenty-four containers. Three of these ten-packs supply thirty, leaving six spares.
Find it again: browse Hit Point Press's Cubeamajigs collection for this set and other decorative designs, or search Cubeamajigs Land Panorama Daarken. Check the artwork and retail quantity on the replacement listing. The advertised “up to 400 cards” refers to the ten-pack's combined unsleeved capacity, not double-sleeved capacity per container.

The calculator's 0.82-inch model gives 25–27 double-sleeved cards by depth. Width is a tighter concern: a 66 mm sleeve would have only 0.18 mm total clearance before molded corners or tolerances. Confirm fit before buying a full collection's supply.
Find it again: search for APACALI 24 Pack Card Deck Box B09CH5VK1G. The original URL contains “0.94” despite the selected item's 0.82-inch title; match the ASIN, pack count, and current dimensions when reordering. See the storage research for the dimension discrepancy.
Slim Jumpstart deck boxes from jman2c on eBay
Compact alternative for twenty-card packs; not selected for the twenty-five-card double-sleeved target. The seller advertises 20+ double-sleeved, 25+ single-sleeved, or 45+ unsleeved cards. No numerical interior dimensions or tested sleeve combination were supplied. These are opaque, latching boxes with interlocking sides and a card-removal slot.
eBay product listing
Seller's other listings
Reorder identifiers: item 227289326606; seller jman2c; search Jumpstart Deck Box Slim Deck Boxes Trading Card Game Cubes 20+ Cards.
On the review date, the listing offered new boxes in multiple colors and quantities of 1, 3, 15, 24, or 36, with more than ten available. That suggests a repeatable product listing rather than a one-off sale, though continued supply is not guaranteed. The seller had 99.6% positive feedback, but the sole feedback entry for this item was an automated delivery note, not a fit or durability review. These details and the capacity claim come from the listing and its seller description.
A matching Etsy listing from UsefulExtrusion had 4.3/5 across seven item reviews, including successful Jumpstart use and an insufficient-capacity report. The seller's response specifies twenty double-sleeved cards, with only one or two more potentially squeezed in. Its title, photos, and description match the eBay product, but the two seller accounts have not been explicitly linked. The UsefulExtrusion shop provides another route to investigate if the item disappears.
Assessment: worth considering for a small twenty-card packet after a sample fit check. It offers no established allowance for five additional double-sleeved cards, and long-term durability remains unverified.
Tools
The Sturdy Deck Press
MakerWorld model and print files by Nabes Teban. A 3D-printable press for removing trapped air from sleeved or double-sleeved cards, suggested for the Jumpstart preparation kit. Cards load from the side; the upper tray attaches to the screw, and an optional lower tray helps with removal.
Print profile: the designer's profile 2018145 specifies 0.2 mm layers, nine walls, and 33% infill. The original design uses ABS; the designer also recommends PETG in the comments. Check the current profile and assembly instructions for the chosen printer and material.
Small-packet fit: the designer confirms that the screw intentionally stops short of the base and suggests adding tokens, lands, or bulk cards when a stack is too short. An individual twenty- or twenty-five-card Jumpstart packet may need that additional stack height. Pressing does not establish a fixed final card thickness; measure the actual packet for the storage calculator.
Find it again: MakerWorld model 1884468, The STURDY DECK PRESS, creator Nabes Teban. The creator's profile provides a fallback if the model URL changes.
Card storage calculator
Open the calculator to work from either a card stack or a box. It supports single and double sleeves, separate compressed and post-play measurements, inserts, padding, removal clearance, and editable box dimensions. The Burger Tokens and APACALI presets connect these saved products to the sizing calculations.
Keeping the list useful
When a link disappears, search the saved product name and identifier, or return to the manufacturer or seller. Confirm dimensions and size variants again before treating a replacement listing as the same product. For a successful purchase, add the chosen size, actual measured interior, sleeve combination, and comfortable card count here so the next order can use a tested fit.

title: Zombies vs Plants — Card Research
text:
Zombies vs Plants — Card Research
Box concept and pairing rule · All research · Researched October 21, 2026
Explore cards and ideas for eight Jumpstart packets: four Plants and four Zombies, and a future cube. This gallery remains a research pool, not a decklist. The boxed-set page contains all eight v0.1 twenty-card lists, including lands, roles, setup, and test notes. The first game has now been played; its interaction findings and candidates are below. Unused candidates stay here for rebalancing. The pictures and Oracle text are sourced from Scryfall; the role, fit, mana, and caution notes are our design judgments.
First playtest: more chances to interact
Browse the interaction shortlist with card images, Oracle text, and individual tradeoffs. These are proposed changes, not replacements already applied to v0.1.
The October 21 game (e7dd2877-c60d-4b18-b5a1-7730d6216636) paired Overgrowth + Spore Swarm against Restless Dead + The Turned. Plants won. Zombies reported sparse interaction and repeated unanswered attacks, rating meaningful choices 4/10; Plants rated its choices 7/10 and highlighted its removal and sacrifice decisions. That difference suggests investigating how readily each side can answer threats, without treating one game as proof of a faction-wide imbalance.
The saved actions and final deck state make the problem more specific:
Plants used Fungal Infection, Feed the Swarm, and Nature's Way to remove successive Zombie blockers. These were already thematic interaction in the original lists.
Zombies' Dead Weight and Ram Through remained undrawn. Eviscerate was milled at revision 61; Return to Nature also remained in the library. The list contained answers, but this game did not put them into hand in time.
Ram Through needs a surviving creature. More spells with that same dependency will not help when every blocker has been removed. A cheap answer usable from an empty battlefield is the first role to test.
Zombies repeatedly spent mana recovering creatures. Recursion can be valuable, but it competes with rebuilding and answering the opponent; adding still more recovery is not the first experiment.
Check feedback claims against card text. Plants' survey says Nature's Way prevented Bayou Groff's combat damage. The supplied card snapshot and current Oracle text give vigilance, trample, and damage to an opposing creature; there is no damage-prevention effect. Its claimed prevention-based invalidation of lethal is unsupported. That does not certify the entire game as error-free. Preserve the original survey as the player's report rather than silently rewriting it into a verified rules finding.
Best candidates for the next revision
Packet
Candidate
What it adds
Proposed comparison
Restless Dead
Infernal Grasp · {1}{B} instant
Broad death magic: destroy a creature and lose 2 life. Works with no creature of your own and only one black mana symbol.
First test: replace Rise from the Grave. Keep Eviscerate, Dead Weight, all eight creatures, and the cheaper recovery cards.
Restless Dead
Tragic Slip · {B} instant
A death turns -1/-1 into -13/-13. Zombie deaths, combat trades, and sacrifices can enable a dramatic answer.
A flavorful alternative experiment, not an unconditional substitute for Eviscerate. Without a death it cannot kill a large threat.
Stitched Together
Chill of the Grave · {2}{U} instant, discounted to {1}{U} with a Zombie
Grave-cold taps a creature, keeps it tapped through its next untap, and draws a card.
Compare with Think Twice: exchange later flashback value for immediate interaction. Blue already has several answers, so this is a later refinement.
Tomb Guard
Desert's Hold · {2}{W} Aura
Tomb/desert restraint stops attacks, blocks, and activated abilities, including a sacrifice engine.
Compare with Unconventional Tactics. The current pack has no Desert, so its conditional life gain is unavailable; the restraint still works.
Overgrowth
Lignify · {1}{G} Aura
Turn a creature into an abilityless base 0/4 Treefolk. Botanical interaction that needs no friendly creature.
Compare with Nature's Way, changing the kind of answer rather than simply giving the winning pair more removal. The opponent keeps a blocker; counters and other modifying effects can still matter.
Ancient Grove
Sundering Growth · {G/W}{G/W} instant
Vegetation destroys an artifact or enchantment, then copies one of your creature tokens if you have one.
Compare with Rootborn Defenses when problematic Auras or engines justify it. Payable with white alone, but two white pips matter with the black partner; it is not a general creature answer.
Start with the one Restless Dead swap, then repeat the same pairing with starting seats reversed. That preserves the creature count and isolates a cheaper, independent answer. Record whether it was drawn, castable when needed, actually used, and enough to create a meaningful choice. A card remaining in the library cannot establish that its rules or mana cost failed. Test the other pairings before applying every suggestion at once.
Reserves and limits
The Turned: Bite Down gives the Zombies another literal bite and could replace Regrowth, but duplicates Ram Through's reliance on a friendly creature. Keep this as a reserve rather than the first fix for an empty board.
Spore Swarm: retain Fungal Infection and Feed the Swarm for the next comparison; they supplied meaningful interaction in this game. Eaten Alive can turn expendable fodder into exile removal, but its sacrifice requirement makes it a conditional alternative. Without a sacrifice, its total cost is {3}{B}{B}, not four mana.
Wild Awakening: Insidious Fungus is a small botanical body with an artifact/enchantment answer or a draw-and-land option. It could replace Return to Nature for a different mix of flexibility and timing, but loses graveyard exile and requires {2} plus sacrificing it to activate. The pack already has Ram Through for creatures.
Ancient Grove: Martyred Rusalka is a cheap tree-associated Spirit that can sacrifice a creature to prevent an enemy creature attacking that turn. Act before attackers are declared; it does not remove an existing attacker from combat. Utopia Vow is a green botanical alternative for Overgrowth: restraint in exchange for giving the enchanted creature a mana ability. Neither needs to displace the grove's preferred ordinary birds.
Bone Splinters has excellent undead flavor, but paying a creature as an additional cost can make the lack-of-blockers problem worse. Protection, recursion, combat tricks, temporary tapping, and removal each supply different decisions; do not count all of them as interchangeable answers to an established threat.
The broader research remains available for the cube. These tests keep the Jumpstart packets monocolor, twenty cards each, and focused on familiar effects.
Shared research for Jumpstart and a future cube
Retain this entire research pool for Jumpstart rebalancing and a future Zombies vs Plants cube, regardless of the first draft's selections. Leaving a candidate out of a draft is not a reason to remove it from the research. Preserve its role, selection concerns, saved Oracle data, images, rulings where available, source queries, theme tags, and mana needs so later revisions can reconsider it. Cards that are too demanding, complex, powerful, or unsuitable for a twenty-card packet remain useful comparisons and possible cube choices. The Necrobloom and other multicolor candidates remain here even if they do not enter the first Jumpstart lists.
Versioned Jumpstart packet lists and a future cube inventory will be separate selections from this shared research. Each Jumpstart revision should record its replacements and reasons without shrinking the candidate pool. No cube size, draft procedure, color distribution, singleton policy, or final card list has been chosen. The Jumpstart same-faction pairing restriction applies to that box; cube drafting and faction restrictions need their own design decision.
Eight-pack shortlist
The packet themes and mana colors are confirmed; names and contents remain provisional. The four Plant themes are Plants, Treefolk, Fungi, and Lands, with suitable Elementals and other creature types mixed in. The Zombie themes are ordinary black necromancy, experiments, ancient tombs, and The Turned. The first Jumpstart box targets simple, easy-to-play mono-color packets. Broader color combinations remain research for the future cube.
Faction
Working pack name
Confirmed mana color
Brief identity
Plants
Overgrowth
Green
Hungry Plants, roots, and vines. Grow and protect a few increasingly dangerous creatures.
Plants
Ancient Grove
White
Stompy Treefolk and botanical support supply the combined deck's larger threats.
Plants
Spore Swarm
Black
Early Fungi, death value, and token production recycle the fallen without requiring green mana.
Plants
Wild Awakening
Green
The landscape joins the fight: animated forests, botanical Elementals, and vegetation brought to life.
Zombies
Restless Dead
Black
Classic necromancy: raise the dead, reuse fallen creatures, and make sacrifice worthwhile.
Zombies
Stitched Together
Blue
Laboratory Zombies assembled from spare parts. Stock the graveyard and build stitched monstrosities.
Zombies
Tomb Guard
White
Mummies and disturbed tomb guardians. Coordinated attacks, protective magic, and carefully chosen embalming effects.
Zombies
The Turned
Green
Zombified plants lead the theme, backed by other green Zombie menaces where useful.
The owner confirmed green Plants, white Treefolk, black Fungi, and green Lands. The Zombie colors remain black, blue, white, and green. The Turned includes botanical undead where practical and other green Zombies where needed. Off-color discoveries remain in the shared research for the cube; they do not change the first Jumpstart box's confirmed directions.
A theme permits creature-type mixing and support spells. White Treefolk is deliberately the stompy half of a combined forty-card deck: it contributes larger threats and support, while the other three Plant packets should provide useful early plays. White can also include cheap botanical helpers and interaction. Test Ancient Grove with Plants, Fungi, and Lands separately; it need not be an independently balanced twenty-card deck. The v0.1 quantities are recorded separately on the boxed-set page; the research pool remains broader than those selections.
Singleton nonbasic variety remains preferred across compatible packets. The owner allows deliberate repeats when a theme has too few suitable cards. Record that reason and test the result. Repeating expensive Treefolk increases their density; it does not create early plays or fix the combined deck's curve.
The gallery's filters are broader research categories, not eight completed packet lists. Plants, Treefolk, Fungi, and Living lands feed the four Plant proposals; Botanical allies supplies case-by-case candidates across them. Supporting spells and appropriately themed Dryads or Elementals can fit without changing their actual creature types.
Faction decision: undead identity takes precedence
Zombified botanical creatures belong to the Zombie faction. A Plant Zombie is an enemy of the living garden, not automatically a candidate for both sides. The same applies to Zombie Treefolk, Zombie Fungi, and botanical Zombie Elementals such as Skullbriar. The Necrobloom is assigned to the Zombie side by its undead theme even though its actual type is Plant.
The browser preserves their botanical research tags so the discoveries remain easy to find, but its faction filter assigns these cards only to Zombies. The featured overlap marker records a botanical/undead combination; it does not indicate dual alignment. Ordinary living Fungi and Saprolings remain eligible for Plants: decomposition or a graveyard mechanic alone does not make a creature undead.
Only packets from the same faction can combine under the box's agreed rule. Faction labels do not grant card types or abilities.
Searching beyond creature types
The research includes creatures, token makers, tribal boosts, and supporting spells. A card does not need Plant, Treefolk, Fungus, or Zombie in its own type line to belong. Look at what it creates, what it helps, and its botanical or undead theme. The card-kind filter can isolate noncreatures; searching the rules text or notes can find token makers and other support.
For botanical discoveries, use these as research directions rather than a new rules classification:
Direction
How we use it
Plant, Treefolk, Fungus, Dryad
Strong places to begin creature research. Preserve the actual Oracle types; botanical flavor does not make a Dryad a Plant.
Saproling and Splinter
Include the cards that create or support these tokens. Token objects are not separate cards to put into a packet. Splintering Wind is one such lead, with significant upkeep and damage drawbacks.
Elemental, Spirit, Nymph, Avatar, Wall
Inspect individual cards for trees, vines, flowers, gardens, or vegetation spirits. Woodvine Elemental and Kodama of the North Tree illustrate why a type-only search misses possibilities.
Golem, Construct, Scarecrow
Consider wooden, wicker, or other botanical materials case by case. Crop guardians are a looser thematic extension, not an adopted packet identity.
Horror, Ooze, Beast, Wurm, Phyrexian, Zombie, and other broad types
Search for specifically botanical members rather than including the whole type. Corrupted growth or reanimated vegetation can be especially useful for this matchup.
Elf, Druid, and other practitioners
A plant-magic support card can fit even when its creature is not botanical. Forest association alone is not enough to include every member.
The Plant wiki and related Spuzzem entry are useful discovery leads, particularly for old names and type changes. Floral Spuzzem, Singing Tree, and Wall of Kelp are recorded with their current Scryfall types and rules, regardless of wording on an old printing. Wiki trivia and visual interpretation guide discovery; Scryfall supplies the card facts.
Some supplied leads needed correction: Nessian Wanderer is a Satyr Scout, not a Nymph or Dryad. An exact Scryfall lookup found no card named Timber Golem. These checks are retained in the search provenance rather than turning an unverified example into a candidate.
Living forests and swamps
Animated forests and swamps are automatic investigation candidates for the Plant faction, regardless of the creature type they gain. The Living lands filter covers land creatures, cards that animate lands, and support that specifically improves land creatures. It now supplies the proposed Wild Awakening packet; the filter remains a broad investigation pool, not its selected contents.
The notes distinguish actual Forest or Swamp subtypes from woodland or marsh flavor. Living Lands animates Forests; Kormus Bell animates Swamps; both affect opponents too. Llanowar Loamspeaker and Sylvan Awakening can animate either kind of land. Hissing Quagmire is a living mire but is not typed as a Swamp, while Treetop Village becomes an Ape and is not typed as a Forest. Those differences matter for card interactions, not for whether we investigate the theme.
Animation can expose the mana base to creature removal, and some effects create complicated interactions. Life and Limb, for example, turns Saprolings into Forest lands as well as animating Forests. Combined with Sporemound, this can repeatedly trigger mandatory token creation. Such cards remain visible with cautions so we can investigate them without silently treating them as suitable starter cards.
Prefer enablers that preserve this identity instead of turning it into an Elf deck. Awakener Druid is a Human Druid that animates a Forest, while Animate Land, Awakening of Vitu-Ghazi, and Brave the Wilds provide spell-based alternatives. Ambush Commander stays in the research as a comparison, but its Elf identity and its conversion of Forests into Elves make it a lower-priority fit. An enabling Druid does not need to be called a plant to justify its support role.
Priority botanical undead
The owner requested all actual Zombie Plants, Zombie Treefolk, and Zombie Fungi as thematic priorities. Every card returned by the explicit creature-type intersection query is included in this snapshot. The browser highlights them and offers a botanical-undead filter. They are priorities for finding a home somewhere in the box, not a requirement to cram every card into every packet.
Actual overlapping types
Cards found
Plant Zombie
Creakwood Ghoul; Dreg Mangler; Shambling Shell; Slitherhead; Vulturous Zombie; Woodwraith Strangler.
Zombie Treefolk
Black Oak of Odunos; Ghoultree.
Zombie Fungus / Fungus Zombie
Deathspore Thallid; Molderhulk; Rhizome Lurcher.
Slitherhead is especially flexible: its single black/green hybrid cost can be paid with either color. Dreg Mangler, in contrast, needs both black and green. A shared creature type does not remove a colored mana requirement. The overlap marker records botanical and undead identity, while its research tags preserve the Plant, Treefolk, or Fungus connection. Its eventual Zombie packet placement remains open.
These undead candidates are reserved for the Zombie side. The same-alignment pairing rule and preference for varied nonbasic cards across compatible packets still apply.
Special mention: The Necrobloom
The Necrobloom is a particularly strong flavor crossover: its actual type is Legendary Creature — Plant, and its landfall ability creates Plants or, once you control seven lands with different names, Zombies instead. It also gives land cards in your graveyard dredge 2. That is a compelling bridge between growth and necromancy without a Zombie type line.
It appears under the Zombie faction with a Botanical undead · flavor marker, separate from the eleven explicit creature-type overlaps above. Its three-color cost and seven-different-land-names condition deserve attention before any packet assignment: seven basic lands with repeated names will not unlock its Zombie tokens. It is a research priority, not yet a commitment to a particular mana base or packet.
Botanical Zombies beyond Plant, Treefolk, and Fungus
Skullbriar, the Walking Grave is another priority flavor crossover. Its roots and overgrowth belong in the botanical investigation even though its actual type is Zombie Elemental. It belongs to the Zombie faction while retaining its Botanical allies research tag. Its black-green cost needs deliberate fixing, and its unusual retention of counters through zone changes is documented with saved rulings in the card details.
The separate Zombie Elemental search also returned Invasion of Azgol // Ashen Reaper. That result was not selected as botanical: a Zombie Elemental type line alone does not establish plant flavor. Keep looking at individual creatures and art rather than restricting this investigation to the three core botanical types.
Proposed Zombie theme: The Turned
The owner proposed The Turned as a green-led Zombie packet identity, particularly for plant-like creatures that have become undead. It is one of the eight shortlisted packet identities; its first green-paid twenty-card list is now recorded on the boxed-set page, while the broader pool remains under investigation. It gives the botanical crossovers a possible home on the Zombie side without displacing the existing black necromancy, blue stitched-creature, or white mummy ideas.
Initial leads include Slitherhead, Dreg Mangler, Shambling Shell, Vulturous Zombie, Woodwraith Strangler, Ghoultree, Molderhulk, Rhizome Lurcher, and Skullbriar. Several of these wider research leads need black as well as green and therefore do not fit the current mono-green Jumpstart target. Slitherhead can be cast entirely with green through its hybrid cost; Ghoultree needs only green. Other green Zombies can fill out the theme. The browser's The Turned research filter groups these leads for investigation without assigning final quantities or a mana base.
The Necrobloom is also a proposed candidate through its flavor and its Plant/Zombie token production, despite not having the Zombie type itself. Its cost is {1}{W}{B}{G}, so a packet containing it must intentionally support white, black, and green. It cannot assume that a white mummy packet will always be its partner. Its seven-differently-named-lands condition remains a separate construction challenge, not something solved merely by adding three colors.
The Necrobloom and optional multicolor upgrades
The Necrobloom stays on the Zombie research wishlist while we build a coherent base box. Casting it needs white, black, and green; a pair of ordinary mono-color packets does not by itself supply all three. Flexible mana sources can supply a third color without changing the game rules, but those sources must actually be included and drawn. Its Zombie-token condition separately requires seven lands with different names, not simply seven lands or three colors. It still makes Plants below that threshold, but that misses much of the desired undead payoff.
A possible later module is a prepared spotlight upgrade selected after the packet pair: one exciting multicolor card accompanied by a fixed list of card and land substitutions, preserving the forty-card deck and recording how to restore both packets. A black-green pair such as Restless Dead + The Turned could be the starting point for a Necrobloom upgrade with white access and an appropriate land package. This is a design direction, not an adopted or playable module: the full replacements, allowed pairs, selection fairness, mana reliability, and power level must be designed and tested first. There is no free casting, command zone, or change to the printed cost proposed here.
A simpler optional pool for two-color cards could work with matching pairs, but a color match alone does not guarantee enough sources or a balanced upgrade. Adding a three-color card alone is not a solution. The base box currently keeps all twenty cards from each packet; any future substitution module must explicitly replace that setup instruction.
Earlier construction alternatives — retained for later
The first prototype now uses simple mono-color packets with the two-packet, forty-card base rules. These earlier alternatives remain recorded for future experiments; they are not active changes to the first box:
Mixed mono-color and two-color packets: choose colors around each theme and include enough fixing for every allowed partner.
All two-color packets: allow two- to four-color combined decks, with greater demands on fixing and early colored costs.
Optional cards after pairing: a possible extra pool of multicolor cards, requiring a complete selection, replacement, mana, and reset procedure.
Three twenty-card packets: sixty-card preassembled decks; larger decks do not by themselves solve color access. With four distinct packets per faction, choosing three creates four combinations per faction, compared with six when choosing two.
Future cube: retain the broader card pool for a separate draftable design; Jumpstart can remain the simpler way to play with the same themes.
Functional checks for simple mono-color packets
These October 21, 2026 checks use current Scryfall Oracle text. They assess what the cards require and how each packet contributes to a combined deck; the subsequent v0.1 lists are now drafted, but have not been playtested. A card should not silently require missing colors or an unsupported mechanic, but each packet need not be a balanced standalone deck. Card quantities in a search are discovery evidence, not proof that all results are suitable.
White Treefolk: confirmed stompy and support role
A Treefolk core supplies the larger threats, backed by botanical creatures, removal, and protection. The other three Plant packets are expected to supply early plays. Cheap white helpers can improve those pairings without changing the packet into a generic small-creature deck or requiring every creature to be a Treefolk.
Indomitable Ancients is a 2/10 for {2}{W}{W} with no abilities. It functions independently but contributes little offensive power.
Old Ghastbark is a 3/6 with no abilities, costing {3}{G/W}{G/W}. It is both green and white as a card, but white mana alone casts it.
Sun-Dappled Celebrant is a 5/6 for {4}{W}{W} with convoke and vigilance. Its payoff is self-contained and it offers a credible attacker; convoke adds a casting decision.
Moonlit Lamenter supplies its own -1/-1 counter and can remove it for a card. It does not require a separate counter engine, but adds bookkeeping, especially alongside +1/+1 counters.
Oaken Brawler and Sentry Oak introduce clash. Sentry Oak repeats that process to attack, making it a lower priority for the simple version.
Flowering of the White Tree is a useful whole-deck buff: its nonlegendary-creature bonus works on Plants, Fungi, animated lands, and tokens as well as Treefolk. Its additional legendary-creature text and two-white cost deserve review.
White has botanical support beyond creatures. Rootborn Defenses protects the board even without a token to populate, but its extra keyword is a complexity cost. Seed Spark needs green mana spent to make its Saprolings, so that token mode must not be assumed in a self-contained white packet. White land-animation spells such as Encircling Fissure exist, but awaken adds more rules than basic protection.
Birds of the canopy
The owner explicitly supports actual birds as inexpensive allies of Treefolk: hawks, falcons, eagles, ravens, and rocs living among the trees. Bird people, avian warriors, and similar humanoids are outside this direction. Ancient Grove keeps its Treefolk identity while birds contribute early bodies, aerial defense, and ways to attack over a crowded ground battlefield. The v0.1 packet now uses one copy of each of the three preferred birds; the other candidates remain available.
Preferred early-bird candidates: Healer's Hawk, Rustwing Falcon, and Suntail Hawk. The owner particularly likes the first two and endorses Suntail as a classic, simple option that allows more distinct cards and fewer duplicates. Its lower stats than Rustwing are an accepted tradeoff for singleton variety. The v0.1 Ancient Grove list includes one of each; further changes will depend on testing the full packet and its pairings.
The owner's white Bird search, bounded to paper/non-funny cards released by October 21, 2026, returned 40 cards at mana value two or less. That includes unsuitable creature identities and mechanics; the saved shortlist is curated rather than an automatic inclusion of every match. Every Bird selected here has the actual type Creature — Bird.
Early bird
Role and limitation
Healer's Hawk
{W}, 1/1, flying and lifelink. Early pressure and life gain with every partner. General power boosts improve both its damage and life gain.
Rustwing Falcon
{W}, 1/2, flying. A particularly simple early body with a little more toughness.
Battlefield Raptor
{W}, 1/2, flying and first strike. Another actual bird; stronger combat options, but first strike adds a damage-step rule and may be potent with buffs.
Suntail Hawk
{W}, 1/1, flying. A preferred classic option for singleton variety. Rustwing has one more toughness, but including distinct birds can avoid repeats while keeping the early plays simple.
Courier Hawk
{1}{W}, 1/2, flying and vigilance. Can attack while remaining available to block, with no partner dependency or additional subsystem.
Territorial Roc
{1}{W}, 1/3, flying. Simple early defense while larger Treefolk develop; only modest offensive power.
Beacon Hawk
{1}{W}, 1/1, flying. Combat damage to a player can untap a creature, including an attacking Treefolk; {W} buys +0/+1 for the turn. More text, and the untap requires connecting rather than working like unconditional vigilance.
Three-mana birds offer more direct support, while remaining above the main early-curve gap:
Keen-Eyed Raven: {2}{W}, 2/2, flying; puts a +1/+1 counter on another creature you control when it enters. Works with a Treefolk or any partner's creature, but cannot put the counter on itself.
Roc Charger: {2}{W}, 1/3, flying; when it attacks, another attacking creature without flying gains flying for the turn. It can help a large Treefolk get past ground blockers. Both must attack, so it does not enable a creature with defender to attack.
Scouting Hawk: {2}{W}, 1/1, flying; can find a basic Plains onto the battlefield tapped on entry if an opponent controls more lands. This is conditional catch-up ramp, not reliable access to a partner's Forest or Swamp, and adds searching and shuffling.
Eagle of the Watch: {2}{W}, 2/1, flying and vigilance. A simple literal eagle alternative; it costs more than the early hawks and remains fragile.
The existing Scion of Vitu-Ghazi lead also makes Bird tokens, giving its botanical Elemental another connection to this canopy theme. Flowering of the White Tree can strengthen both birds and Treefolk. Test flying pressure against each Zombie pairing and retain enough large Treefolk for the packet's identity to remain clear.
Some cheap Birds carry unsuitable dependencies: Glint Hawk needs an artifact to return; War Falcon needs a Knight or Soldier to attack; Squadron Hawk needs deliberate extra copies to use its search ability. Ranger's Hawk adds dungeon rules, and Duskrider Falcon's protection from black is unusually targeted at this opposing faction. None is a default early-body inclusion merely because its cost is low.
Cheap botanical helpers to compare
These are candidates, not selected additions or a reason to fill the packet with unrelated white creatures.
The owner explicitly includes Nymphs and Dryads as nature-spirit allies of the grove, with suitable Druids and individual Spirits alongside them. The theme can connect small forest guardians to large Treefolk without requiring every creature to share a type. Artwork and flavor can establish a fit even for a Wall; preserve actual Oracle types and distinguish a meaningful grove connection from incidental trees in a background.
Candidate
Early role and limitation
Juniper Order Rootweaver
A 2/2 Human Druid for {1}{W}, the clearest new early practitioner lead. Its optional {G} kicker adds a +1/+1 counter to an allied creature; the basic body works without green, so that bonus is useful with a green partner rather than required.
Alseid of Life's Bounty
A 1/1 Nymph for {W} with lifelink, explicitly endorsed for the nature-spirit theme. Pay {1} and sacrifice it to protect an allied creature or enchantment from a chosen color. Useful with every partner; protection has targeting and Aura consequences.
Dryad Militant
A 2/1 Dryad Soldier payable with {W} alone. It gives an immediate body, but its global instant/sorcery exile can interfere with either player's spell recursion or flashback.
Mycologist
A 0/2 Human Druid for {1}{W} that cultivates Saprolings and sacrifices them for life. It starts as a small blocker; natural token production takes three upkeeps and introduces spore counters.
Scarecrow Guide
A 2/1 colorless Scarecrow for {2} with reach. Once each turn it can convert one generic mana into a mana of any color; this is filtering, not ramp. A crop guardian is a looser thematic helper, not a plant creature.
Kami of False Hope
A 1/1 Spirit for {W}, nominated for its tree-like spiritual imagery. Sacrifice it without a mana payment to prevent all combat damage that turn, including your own. An inexpensive way to buy time for larger creatures or token engines.
Angelic Wall
A 0/4 Wall for {1}{W} with flying and defender. The owner's forest-and-spiritual-wings interpretation makes it a grove guardian candidate despite its type. A substantial early blocker with no partner dependence; it cannot attack.
Martyred Rusalka
A 1/1 Spirit for {W}, whose flavor explicitly connects its ghost to the Tree of Weeping. Pay {W} and sacrifice a creature to stop a target creature attacking that turn. Can use fungal fodder; activate before attackers are declared, since it does not remove an already-attacking creature.
Candlegrove Witch
A 2/2 Human Warlock for {1}{W}, a grove-practitioner lead. Coven can grant it flying at the beginning of combat if three creatures have different powers. The base body works with every partner; the bonus adds a power-counting check.
Juniper Order Rootweaver remains functional with black Fungi: {1}{W} buys its 2/2 body; only the optional kicker needs green. The owner's other Juniper link points to Juniper Order Advocate, although its visible label names Juniper Order Druid. Advocate is a white 1/2 for {2}{W} that boosts green creatures while it is untapped. It is more partner-dependent: black Fungi can produce green Saprolings for it to boost, but white Treefolk and black Fungus bodies receive no bonus. The actual Druid is a separate green 1/1 for {2}{G} that taps to untap a land, not a white candidate.
Mycologist also connects the themes without requiring green mana: black cards can produce green Saprolings for its life-gain ability, and its own Saprolings can feed the black packet's general sacrifice effects. That makes it worth investigating at low power, while its slow output remains a real limitation.
The owner's tree-art and forest-art searches are complementary discovery tools. With paper, non-funny, and October 21, 2026 cutoff filters, they returned 64 and 22 cards respectively, with 76 distinct cards combined. Only selected thematic leads enter this research; a tree in the background is not an automatic inclusion. Art searches also depend on printing: the forest search returned the Portal Second Age Angelic Wall by Rebecca Guay, while the tree search returned the Tenth Edition version by John Avon. Both discoveries are recorded; the gallery uses the forest-search printing, without assuming which illustration the owner meant.
Three-mana nature spirits
These broaden the grove's support choices but do not fill the one- and two-mana gap:
Harvestguard Alseids is a 2/3 Nymph for {2}{W}. Its constellation ability triggers on its own arrival as well as other enchantments: play it before combat to prevent damage to an existing attacker that turn. It does not need flash for that use. Hoofprints, Flowering, and other enchantments can trigger it again, but it prevents damage rather than every kind of removal.
Observant Alseid is a 2/2 Nymph with vigilance for {2}{W}. Its optional {4}{W} bestow can strengthen a creature from either packet without requiring an enchantment-focused deck. The costs and creature/Aura rules make it a lower priority for the simple prototype.
Beckoning Will-o'-Wisp is a 1/3 flying Spirit for {2}{W}. The owner's proposed flavor is a wisp luring enemies into the Treefolk's grove. Choosing an opponent at the beginning of combat gives creatures attacking that player +1/+0, supporting either large Treefolk or a wider partner board. In multiplayer, the bonus is not restricted to your creatures.
Starfield Mystic is a lower-priority practitioner because its payoff needs enough enchantments and its type alone does not establish botanical flavor. Prepared-card mechanics on Emergency Phytomedic are also outside the simplest early-helper direction.
White does have a literal Fungus: Pallid Mycoderm, a 2/4 for {3}{W}. Its spore-counter and Saproling-sacrifice abilities are relevant research, but it is not an inexpensive answer to the early curve. This does not change the confirmed black Fungus packet.
User-nominated botanical support and Elemental leads
These nominations broaden the theme beyond literal Treefolk. They are research candidates; no illustration details or packet slots are assumed.
Hoofprints of the Stag costs {1}{W} and is an owner-endorsed repeatable token engine for the white grove. It works with every partner and can benefit from extra card draw, including black Fungi's draw effects. As a kindred enchantment, it is something to cast early but not an immediate blocker: each activation needs four hoofprint counters accumulated from draws and {2}{W}, during its controller's turn.
Beza, the Bounding Spring is a 4/5 for {2}{W}{W}. Its four catch-up checks are independent, covering opposing lands, life, creatures, and cards in hand. More than one benefit can occur; the comparisons and potential token types add complexity rather than guaranteeing one fixed entry effect.
Scion of Vitu-Ghazi is a 4/4 for {3}{W}{W}. When cast from hand, its entry ability makes a flying Bird and then populates. It supplies its own token to copy, or can copy an existing creature token from the partner packet; it does not require that partner to make its first token. The cast-from-hand condition matters for reanimation.
These larger cards are possible threats and support for a combined deck. They do not resolve the early curve by themselves, and repeating them would not change that.
Black Fungi: self-contained without green
Black can create its own fungal bodies and sacrifice fodder. A token being green does not require spending green mana to create it.
Deathbloom Thallid costs {2}{B}; its death creates a green Saproling.
Fungal Infection costs {B}, gives a creature -1/-1 for the turn, and creates a green Saproling.
Synapse Necromage leaves two black Fungus tokens that cannot block. They are not Saprolings.
Thallid Soothsayer can sacrifice any creature to draw; Thallid Omnivore can sacrifice any other creature for its power boost, with extra life only for a Saproling.
Deathcap Marionette contributes an early deathtouch body and optional milling. Mold Folk can use either kind of token for its growth ability.
This supports a simple death-and-regrowth identity without requiring the slow spore-counter system or a green Fungus partner. Limit simultaneous sacrifice outlets and distinguish token types. Deathspore Thallid remains on the Zombie side. Descend, transforming cards, and larger recursive engines can remain cube candidates.
Black Treefolk: independent, but slower and more mechanically demanding
Black Poplar Shaman can regenerate itself; another Treefolk is not required, though regeneration adds rules.
Fendeep Summoner animates Swamps, so black supplies the resource it needs. Land-creature timing and exposure to removal add complexity.
Witherbloom Pledgemage is a 5/5 payable entirely with black. Its life-gain bonus uses instant/sorcery spells rather than more Treefolk.
Sapling of Colfenor is payable with black and its attack trigger works with any creature card, but adds reveal and life-total arithmetic.
Reaping Willow supplies its own counters and can reanimate any creature with mana value three or less. Three black pips at four mana and -1/-1-counter handling are practical concerns.
Thorntooth Witch rewards later Treefolk spells, so it is less reliable in a packet with few Treefolk and a differently themed partner. Weed-Pruner Poplar has a mandatory upkeep target and may have to target a friendly creature.
The examined black-payable Treefolk begin at three mana. Black Treefolk remains useful comparison and cube research; it does not replace the confirmed white Treefolk and black Fungus directions. Black Oak of Odunos is excluded from the Plant faction because it is a Zombie. Boggart Loggers is a Goblin Rogue, not a Treefolk, and its Treefolk/Forest destruction does not make it a suitable botanical inclusion.
The Turned: a thin theme may justify deliberate repeats
Slitherhead, Sultai Devotee, and Ghoultree are the clearest initial green-paid Zombie anchors. Ghoultree needs creature cards in the graveyard to become affordable; scavenge and recovery remove those cards, so their interaction needs testing. Sultai Devotee's mana ability filters mana rather than ramping it.
A deliberate repeat is allowed if the green Zombie theme has too few suitable cards, while singleton variety remains preferred. The v0.1 list uses this exception for two Slitherheads and two Sultai Devotees; the other nonbasics remain singleton within the Zombie faction. Choose repeats for the actual missing role: more expensive threats do not supply early plays. Supporting spells such as Grapple with the Past, Mulch, and Regrowth support the graveyard plan without substituting ordinary living Fungi for Zombies.
Sludge Titan is also payable entirely with green, but repeated milling of five cards is consequential in a forty-card deck. Radiation cards, The Foretold Soldier's repeated foretell process, and elaborate Zombie-copy mechanics are lower priorities for the simple prototype. They remain research candidates for the future cube.
What to investigate before choosing cards
Mana across all pairings
The first Jumpstart shortlist uses the confirmed mono-color directions; the wider shared research retains multicolor possibilities for the cube and later experiments. Inspect every pair separately, including spells that are only useful when cast early. Ancient Grove can rely on the intended early-game contribution of any of its three partners, but mandatory color costs cannot rely on drawing one specific fixing card from one specific partner.
The mana-cost symbols are the starting point. The browser's color filter describes the card's actual colors, not which mana is sufficient to cast it.
Hybrid symbols offer alternatives; ordinary multicolor costs require every shown color. Activated abilities, alternate costs, and second faces also matter.
Creature-only fixing such as a land naming one creature type may not cast supporting spells or the partner's other creature type.
Flexible lands that enter tapped improve color access but can slow early turns. These are candidates to compare, not a chosen land package.
The Turned must work on green mana in the first box. Hybrid costs can be payable entirely with green even when the card itself has two colors; off-color activated abilities and mandatory costs still need checking. This is a mana-construction criterion, not Commander color identity.
Useful partners, not isolated piles
Look for growth spells that work on any creature, token makers that feed sacrifice outlets, recursion that recovers a partner's creatures, and interaction that prevents a battlefield stall. Narrow bonuses need enough targets: a Fungus/Saproling bonus does not strengthen every Plant or Treefolk, and a Zombie bonus does not help a non-Zombie merely because it is in the same faction.
White Treefolk deliberately occupies the expensive end of the combined curve. The Plants, Fungi, and Lands packets should each provide early plays so that all three pairings with it function, with cheap white helpers and interaction considered where useful. Some Fungus engines take time to produce spores, and blue Zombies may consume graveyard cards that black wants to recover. Test each actual pair's combined plan without requiring either twenty-card half to do every job independently.
Balance and complexity
Compare early participation, interaction, ways to finish, and how long engines take to matter. Mark demanding mechanics and exceptionally strong cards instead of assuming a thematic match is automatically a balanced choice. For example, protection from Zombies on Grave Bramble is unusually relevant in this particular matchup. The browser retains cautions alongside candidates so they can be reviewed before selection.
Sources and coverage
Card facts were retrieved through the project's Scryfall MCP server. Each entry links a specific printing and preserves its Oracle text and faces. Art loads from Scryfall's image service; text and research notes come from the saved local snapshot, so browsing and filtering do not repeatedly query the card API.
The eleven type crossovers are complete for the recorded explicit-type query, which excluded funny-format cards and limited results to paper cards released by October 21, 2026. Flavor crossovers such as The Necrobloom are assessed separately. The query intentionally does not count generic changelings as thematic crossover discoveries. Other packet pools are curated starting research, not exhaustive lists of every card or artwork that could fit. New cards and revised Oracle text can change future results.
Download the research snapshot as JSON or inspect the saved search provenance. Exact names, types, full rules text, mana costs, card images, group labels, and individual notes are retained for extending this research or reviewing it in another chat.
